Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

osmnxr 0.1.5

  • New ox_blend() blends point locations — or a whole second graph — into a street network (#6, requested by @talegari), the osmnxr counterpart of sfnetworks::st_network_blend(): each point is snapped onto its nearest edge (grid-indexed planar search in the Rust core) and the edge is split there, in both directions of a two-way street, turning the location into a routable node. Attributes are preserved (length recomputed; travel_time / penalty rescaled proportionally), points beyond tolerance are skipped with a warning, and meta$blend maps every input to its node. Given a second osm_graph, the three-step recipe from the issue is applied: blend its nodes in, stack the graphs with ox_union(), and add connector edges between each snapped pair — one routable multimodal network.

  • New ox_route_shortest() rounds out the ox_route_* family (#5 feedback, @talegari): the sf interface to shortest-path routing, returning cost, node path and merged street geometry per route, with k > 1 enumerating loopless alternatives (Yen) — one naming scheme and one return shape across ox_route_shortest(), ox_route_constrained(), ox_route_pareto() and ox_route_tsp(). ox_shortest_path() and ox_k_shortest_paths() remain as the lighter node-sequence variants.

  • Repeated routing calls on the same graph are much faster (#5 feedback, @talegari): the structural edge index that every router marshals for the Rust core (the dominant per-call cost on metro-sized graphs) is now cached for the session, content-addressed by the graph’s node ids and edge endpoints — so copies hit, edits miss, and nothing goes stale. On the NCR Delhi network (2.1M directed edges) a warm ox_route_constrained() call drops from ~0.7 s to the Rust solve time itself. ox_clear_cache() also clears this cache. The Dijkstra/Yen solvers additionally return the edges they traversed, so ox_route_shortest() and ox_route_tsp() draw exact geometry across parallel edges (previously ox_route_tsp() drew the minimum-weight twin).

  • New preference-aware routing (#5, requested by @talegari): ox_route_constrained() finds the exact minimum-cost route whose consumption of a second edge criterion stays within a budget (e.g. “the shortest route using at most 500 m of residential streets”), and ox_route_pareto() enumerates the full Pareto front of cost-vs-preference trade-offs. Both run on a bicriteria label-setting solver (Martins’ algorithm) with dominance pruning and reverse-Dijkstra bounds in the Rust core — exact, deterministic, one-way streets respected. The new helper ox_add_edge_penalties() builds the penalty/resource edge column from OSM highway classes; added onto the routing weight it also covers simple scalarized (“soft preference”) routing through ox_shortest_path().

  • ox_route_constrained(method = "lagrangian") adds a Lagrangian-relaxation solver (the LARAC algorithm) beside the exact one: the budget constraint is dualized so each iteration is a plain Dijkstra on weight + lambda * resource, which scales to networks where the exact front grows too large. The route returned is always feasible and carries a proven lower_bound on the optimal cost (cost == lower_bound certifies optimality; a message reports any duality gap). The exact method now also reports lower_bound, always equal to cost (#5).

  • Route geometry reconstruction is dramatically faster on large graphs. The bicriteria routers now receive the traversed edge indices straight from the Rust solvers, so no parallel-edge lookup is needed at all — and the geometry is exact even across parallel edges that differ in cost or resource (previously the minimum-weight twin was drawn). On the NCR Delhi drive network (1.0M nodes / 2.1M directed edges) an ox_route_constrained() query runs in ~0.7 s and a 9-route ox_route_pareto() front in ~1.5 s, down from ~16 s and ~140 s. For ox_route_tsp(), the parallel-edge lookup is now built once per call instead of once per leg (and sorts numerically instead of by string key).

osmnxr 0.1.4

  • New ox_route_tsp() solves a travelling-salesman route through a set of stops over the street network, in the spirit of sfnetworks::st_network_travel(): the asymmetric network-distance matrix (one-way streets respected) is computed in the Rust core, the visiting order is solved there too with an iterated local search (or-opt + swap + 2-opt descent restarted from double-bridge perturbations, deterministic), and each leg is returned as an sf row with its cost, node path and street geometry. Supports closed tours (end = start, the default), open routes (end = NULL) and a pinned final stop. Benchmarked against TSP::solve_TSP() (the backend of sfnetworks::st_network_travel()) on identical cost matrices over the bundled real networks, it matched or beat it in all 80 random instances tried (8–50 stops), by ~1% on average at 8 stops up to ~10% at 50 (#4, requested by @talegari).

osmnxr 0.1.3

  • ox_graph_from_*() is dramatically faster on large areas: building the graph from the Overpass response was quadratic in the number of edges (it never finished on a metro-sized bbox) and is now vectorised — a response with 600,000 nodes / 1 million directed edges parses in ~15 s (#3, reported by @talegari).

  • Overpass and Nominatim requests now retry on HTTP 500, 502 and 504 (and on connection failures) in addition to httr2’s default 429/503, with exponential backoff. The number of attempts remains configurable via ox_settings(max_tries = ) (#2, reported by @talegari).

osmnxr 0.1.2

CRAN release: 2026-10-19

  • New ox_union() combines two or more osm_graph objects into one: node and edge tables are stacked, nodes sharing an osmid are merged and edges duplicated across graphs are dropped (dedupe_edges = FALSE keeps them). Attribute columns present in one graph but not another are filled with NA. Designed for multimodal networks — union a street graph with a hand-built layer (e.g. metro) whose transfer edges reference street-node osmids, then route across both (#1, requested by @talegari).

osmnxr 0.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-07-05

  • Fix installation on Windows (R-devel). The rextendr 0.5.0 Makevars templates ran an unnecessary install-time cargo run --bin document step that failed on Windows (os error 193 while running a build script). The extendr wrappers are pre-generated and shipped, so installation only needs cargo build --lib; the document step has been removed from Makevars.in / Makevars.win.in.

osmnxr 0.1.0

First public release of OSMnx for R.

  • ox_example() loads a small bundled real network (central Olinda, Brazil) so examples and vignettes show real analyses offline. The vignettes were reworked around real cases from Boeing (2025) and the OSMnx examples gallery: multi-city orientation entropy (Chicago/New Orleans/Rome), betweenness chokepoints, travel-time routing and isochrones, and amenity accessibility.

  • ox_orientation_entropy() and ox_plot_orientation() now accept either an osm_graph or a numeric vector of bearings.

  • ox_plot_figure_ground() draws figure-ground diagrams, and ox_example() now also bundles "manhattan" and "rome" networks for the new “Figure-ground diagrams” vignette (Boeing 2025, Fig. 3).

  • ox_simplify() now preserves traversability per direction, emitting bidirectional edges for two-way streets (fixes zero-valued routing/centrality on simplified graphs).

  • Download street networks from OpenStreetMap (ox_graph_from_place(), ox_graph_from_address(), ox_graph_from_point(), ox_graph_from_bbox()) via the Overpass API, returning the tidy sf-backed osm_graph object.

  • Geocoding with Nominatim (ox_geocode(), ox_geocode_to_sf()).

  • Rust compute core (via extendr): CSR graph, Dijkstra routing (ox_shortest_path(), ox_distances(), ox_nearest_nodes()) and metrics (ox_basic_stats(), ox_bearings(), ox_orientation_entropy()).

  • example_osm_graph() synthetic grid for offline examples and tests.

  • Configuration via ox_settings() and session caching with ox_clear_cache().

  • Topology cleanup (Rust core): ox_simplify() merges chains of interstitial degree-2 nodes into single edges; ox_consolidate_intersections() merges nearby nodes into one (via connected components); ox_nearest_edges() finds the closest edge to a point.

  • Advanced routing (Rust core): ox_k_shortest_paths() (Yen’s algorithm), ox_distance_matrix() (many-to-many), and ox_isochrone() (reachable-area polygons via multi-source Dijkstra + concave hull).

  • Travel-time routing: ox_add_edge_speeds() and ox_add_edge_travel_times() add speed_kph / travel_time edge columns for time-weighted shortest paths and isochrones.

  • New vignette: “Routing and isochrones”.

  • Network metrics (Rust core): ox_centrality() (betweenness via Brandes’ algorithm, closeness) and ox_circuity() (street straightness). Circuity is now also reported by ox_basic_stats().

  • Interoperability: ox_as_sfnetwork(), ox_as_tidygraph() and ox_as_dodgr() hand the graph to the wider R network ecosystem.

  • Export and persistence: ox_to_geojson(), ox_to_maplibre() (style fragment), and ox_save_graphml() / ox_load_graphml() for a lossless round-trip (edge geometry stored as WKT), compatible with OSMnx / NetworkX / Gephi.

  • Feature downloads: ox_features_from_place() and ox_features_from_bbox() fetch POIs, buildings and amenities from OpenStreetMap as tidy sf points.

  • ox_plot_orientation() draws a polar rose plot of street bearings (ggplot2).

  • Documentation: vignettes “Urban metrics”, “Street orientation”, “Features and points of interest”, “Interoperability and export” and “Accessibility analysis”; full pkgdown reference and articles menu.
